closing.content: The analysis identifies distinct temporal signatures in reported outbreak surveillance across the selected disease families. The strongest patterns are descriptive: Dengue shows a pronounced June–October concentration; ADD combines seasonal event concentration with case-volume divergence; Malaria shows a May–July event concentration and district reporting concentration; Food Poisoning is sensitive to large individual reports; Chikungunya shows a more diffuse profile. The findings are useful for understanding surveillance patterns, but they should not be interpreted as population incidence or causal disease-risk estimates.
